$comment: Continuous sounds of the active vessel's environment. aero: boundary-layer wind (level 20 log10(q / qRef) dB, brightness from Mach) and transonic buffet (Gaussian in Mach around machCenter, modulated rumble). reentry: shock-layer roar and plasma hiss from aero.plasmaIntensity, a buffet rumble that also follows the g-load. Both are airborne for an outside listener and hull-borne (low-passed at hullCutoffHz) inside the cabin. turbulence = depth of the slow random amplitude modulation g (1 + depth x), x the average of two coprime value-noise buffers (RMS 0.35, bounded to [-1, 1]). ambience: the air and sea around the listener, one bed per surface ('water' when the active vessel floats, else 'land'), scaled by (listener pressure / sea level)^pressureGainExponent (silent in vacuum) and, for land, faded out between surfaceAltitude[0] and [1] m of radar altitude; inside the cabin heard through the hull (hullGainDb, hullCutoffHz). cabin: interior ambience (fans, pumps, airflow, 400 Hz power hum) heard only by an interior listener, and structural creaks whose Poisson rate follows g-load, its rate of change and sunlight changes (thermal creaks); creaks use a seeded generator so renders are reproducible.
